title: Voyager Technologies Griffin-1 lander completes environmental testing at NASA JPL
excerpt: The lunar lander passed simulations of space conditions and launch vibrations at the agency's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
bodyHtml:
NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory announced on October 13, 2026, that the Voyager Technologies Griffin-1 lunar lander has completed a series of environmental tests. The spacecraft was put through weeks of tests to show it can survive the conditions of launch through lunar landing.

Engineers subjected the 2,789-pound (1,265-kilogram) spacecraft to vibration testing and acoustic testing. Giant horns powered by compressed gaseous nitrogen blasted the spacecraft with up to 153 decibels inside a sealed acoustic chamber at JPL. Additionally, the lander spent about two weeks in a thermal vacuum chamber, where it alternately baked at up to 167 degrees Fahrenheit (75 degrees Celsius) and froze at temperatures as low as minus 148 F (minus 100 C).

The Griffin-1 spacecraft will carry 10 science and technology demonstrations from six countries. After proving its mettle at JPL, Griffin-1 has returned to Voyager Lunar Systems’ facility for final assembly. Next up: launch-readiness operations before shipment to Cape Canaveral.
topic: NASA JPL Testing Readies Voyager Technologies Lander for Moon Mission
